# Savvy

> Savvy is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS meeting assistant. It prepares a brief from your own source documents, then offers source-grounded guidance during a live conversation: what to say, what to avoid, and which file says so.

Savvy runs on your Mac. Nothing joins the call. It captures your microphone and the system audio of whatever app is playing the other side (Zoom, Meet, Teams, or a phone call routed through the Mac), so no extra participant appears. It is a small always-on-top panel that shows in a screen share like any other window; it is not hidden and does not try to be.

## What it does

- Reads the documents you point it at, read-only, and builds a versioned meeting brief: objective, both positions, priorities, agenda, questions to ask, facts with sources, concessions, red lines, prohibited claims, unauthorised commitments, risks.
- During the call it thinks for three reasons only: the other side asked a question, someone touched a red line from the brief, or you pressed Advice. Between those it runs a silent scan of the last minute of conversation against the brief and shows a "Savvy noticed" card only when something concrete turns up.
- Every card says what to say, what to avoid, and which file says so, with a computed grounding percentage. Low-grounding automatic cards are rejected before they are shown.
- Transcription language is selectable, multi-language by default; the response language is a separate setting on the brief.

## Requirements and constraints

- macOS 13 or newer on Apple Silicon. Intel is buildable from source but unsupported.
- Transcription requires a Deepgram or AssemblyAI account. Meeting audio is streamed to that provider under your own key; there is no offline transcription mode. Savvy sets Deepgram's mip_opt_out=true.
- Recommendations are generated by a CLI already installed and signed in on the Mac: Claude Code or the Codex CLI. Savvy has no model of its own and no paid tier. Excerpts, the brief, and recent transcript turns reach that provider under your own account and terms.
- Source documents are never copied. Derived chunks live in a private local SQLite database. Provider keys live in the macOS Keychain. Audio and transcripts are deleted after 30 days.
